news.title: AI is forcing researchers to confront the possibility of artificial minds
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print What is it like to be a bot? luciano de polo stokkete/Alamy Can minds exist without bodies? Until a couple of years ago, neuroscientist and philosopher Tom Froese rejected the idea of free-floating intelligence, believing – along with many others in his field – that thinking and awareness require learning through physical experience of the world.

“Things are happening that nobody expected,” says Froese. “I realised that not just me, but my whole community, was wrong.” Earlier this month, he invited researchers from fields including neuroscience, robotics and artificial life to the International Conference on Embodied Cognitive Science to assess the fallout.

news.title: An atom-sized black hole could force an entire star to explode
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print A tiny black hole could gobble up a star Elen/Alamy Even an atom-sized black hole could dramatically devour a star. These exotic hypothetical objects, called primordial black holes, would be too small to spot, but thanks to simulations of how they might interact with stars, we now know how researchers might be able to find them.
If we did find them, it could finally shine some light on the makeup of dark matter. In the moments after the big bang, quantum fluctuations could have caused the formation of minuscule black holes.

news.title: Insects once had 24 legs
paras: This illustration depicts Chosha praecursor , a 324-million-year-old early insect with 24 legs. The ancient oddball gives scientists another view into the evolutionary path insects took as they moved from water to land. Insects are famous for their six-legged bodies.

A 324-million-year-old fossil dug up in west Texas had a different setup. This ancient curiosity sported a whopping 18 extra legs along its belly. That’s a body plan unlike any of today’s insects. It is one of the oddest insects ever found , the researchers say.

news.title: November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos)
paras: From the skyscrapers of New York to the ancient Parthenon in Athens, the Beaver Moon supermoon put on a spectacular show for skywatchers around the world. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it!

Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names , often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze.

sport.title: Why Carlos Alcaraz should withdraw from the Davis Cup and focus on the 2027 ATP season
paras: Carlos Alcaraz is currently preparing to compete in the 2026 Davis Cup Finals. The ATP Finals champion has joined the Spanish team in Bologna, Italy, and they will face Austria in the quarter-finals later this week.

Alcaraz will compete for his first Davis Cup title alongside Rafael Jodar, Daniel Merida, Pedro Martinez and Marcel Granollers. Alcaraz’s participation in the Davis Cup Finals has stirred up some controversy with regard to his long-term health and fitness. Should the 23-year-old be competing in such an event so soon after a worrying injury scare?

sport.title: November 25, 1999: The day Agassi was crowned year-end world No 1, two years after dropping out of the top 100
paras: On this day, November 25, 1999, Andre Agassi beat Gustavo Kuerten in straight sets to secure the year-end world No 1 ranking On this day, November 25, 1999, Andre Agassi defeated Gustavo Kuerten in the last round-robin match of the ATP Tour World Championships (6-4, 7-5).

Hard to believe, considering that only two years before, Agassi had dropped down to world No 141 before making his way back to the top. Andre Agassi, the Las Vegas Kid, was also a tennis legend. This title was followed by the 1994 US Open and the 1995 Australian Open , the only time he beat his long-time rival, Pete Sampras, in a Grand Slam final (4-6, 6-1, 7-6, 6-4).

sport.title: Lars Graff: “Beijing wants Grand Slam standards – and Chinese fans love Sinner the way England loved Borg”
paras: “Here we are with one of the most famous umpires in the history of tennis.” Ubaldo Scanagatta’s introduction was no exaggeration. Lars Graff was in the chair for the 2009 Wimbledon men’s final, when Roger Federer beat Andy Roddick 16-14 in the fifth set, and again for the 2012 ladies’ final, won by Serena Williams against Agnieszka Radwanska.

That made the Swede the only international chair umpire of the modern era to officiate both Wimbledon singles finals. In 2020 he moved to the other side of the net, as co-tournament director of the China Open in Beijing.

sport.title: Feliciano Lopez gives his verdict on Carlos Alcaraz and Spain’s chances of winning the Davis Cup this year
paras: Carlos Alcaraz will look to guide Spain to their first Davis Cup title since 2019 this week. Spain have been drawn against Austria in the quarter-finals.

Alcaraz isn’t expected to play singles, with captain David Ferrer opting to rest him unless he’s needed for the deciding doubles tie. The Spanish number one would then return for his nation’s semi-final tie, where he could play two-time Grand Slam champion Alexander Zverev in an ATP Finals final rematch. Spain are among the favourites for the title in Bologna, but can they go all the way?

sport.title: Coco Gauff’s old coach proposes new tennis rule which would make doubles more exciting to watch
paras: The ATP Tour and its doubles players have butted heads throughout the majority of 2026. Friction first arose when the ATP announced proposed reforms to the doubles circuit, reforms that include halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20 per cent to 10 per cent.

Doubles players have pushed back on these proposed changes – over 150 men’s doubles players wrote an open letter to the governing body, urging the Tour to rethink the changes. The ATP Tour board are set to make a final decision – regarding the potential changes – next month.

sport.title: Arthur Rinderknech Maintains Innocence Over Allegedly Refusing Doping Test
paras: Arthur Rinderknech has denied any wrongdoing after being notified that he refused to undergo an anti-doping test earlier this year. 57 is understood to have allegedly refused to submit a sample during an unannounced visit by officials in June in Brittany, France.

Newspaper L’Equipe, which was the first to report this case, said there might have been a possible misunderstanding between Rinderknech and the anti-doping agent. He was first notified of being charged with refusing a test in September, shortly before France’s Davis Cup tie with Canada. Unannounced anti-doping visits are part of tennis’ anti-doping programme.
